item.title: Official Python SDK Released for the Scrapfly Platform
item.description:
Official Python SDK Released for the Scrapfly Platform

The official Python SDK for the Scrapfly platform has been released, providing tools for web scraping, screenshots, AI extraction, crawling, and a remote anti-bot browser.

🧩 Overview

  • Integrates with Scrapy, LlamaIndex, and LangChain.
  • Covers Scrapfly API endpoints including web scraping, screenshots, AI extraction, crawling, and a remote anti-bot browser.
  • Features optional installation extras for added capabilities and performance.

⚙️ Key details

  • AsyncScrapflyClient added in 1.0.0 provides every method of ScrapeClient as coroutines, with streamed methods (scrape_batch, crawl_prompt) as async iterators.
  • Up to 0.12, ScrapflyClient runs a call as a coroutine with async_scrape, async_screenshot, and async_extraction, while concurrent_scrape is an async generator.
  • The unblocker parameter (previously named asp) turns on anti-bot bypass for blocking solutions such as Cloudflare, DataDome, PerimeterX, or Akamai.

🚀 Availability

Extra Purpose
speedups Brotli compression and msgpack serialization
parser Built-in HTML parser (lxml, beautifulsoup4, extruct)
scrapy Scrapy integration
browser Playwright-based cloud browser helpers
browser-use Browser-use agent integration
webhook-server Native webhook server using flask
concurrency Kept for compatibility; concurrency needs no extra dependency
  • The speedups and webhook-server extras install brotli (CPython) or brotlicffi.
  • Up to 0.12 they installed the archived brotlipy, requiring users to run pip uninstall brotlipy before upgrading.

#Python #WebScraping #Scrapfly #Automation #SDK

Source: scrapfly/python-scrapfly

item.title: Python Solver Wins SOICT 2026 Integrated Transportation Contest
item.description:
Python Solver Wins SOICT 2026 Integrated Transportation Contest

A single‑file Python solver was submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup‑and‑delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis.

🔍 Overview

The contest task involved integrating passenger and parcel transportation under constraints of time windows, open routes, and heterogeneous taxi fleets.

🧩 How it Works

The solver combines:

  • A constant‑time insertion test based on latest‑arrival slack.
  • Greedy insertion.
  • Local search.
  • Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated‑annealing acceptance.
  • An exact route‑selection engine.
Component Description
Constant‑time insertion test Based on latest‑arrival slack
Greedy insertion
Local search
ALNS with simulated‑annealing acceptance
Exact route‑selection engine Enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set‑packing problem by branch‑and‑bound strengthened with route‑based large neighborhood search, Lagrangian bounds and reduced‑cost fixing

⚙️ Key details

  • The exact engine is chosen automatically from the instance size.
  • An independent verifier and a watchdog guarantee that a valid answer is always printed.
  • Official evaluation: 38 scored instances, 5‑minute limit, total benefit 487,237.
  • Every run finished within 277 seconds, using at most 279 MB.
  • 28 of the 38 instances terminated well before the limit.

#SOICT #Python #Routing #ALNS #Optimization

Source: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem

item.title: Python SDK for Model Context Protocol Released
item.description:
Python SDK for Model Context Protocol Released

The official Python SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients has been released, providing a Python implementation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The documentation is available at https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/, including a Get started guide, What’s new in v2, the API reference, and a migration guide.

🔍 Overview

  • The Model Context Protocol lets you build servers that expose data and functionality to LLM applications in a secure, standardized way.
  • Think of it like a web API, but designed for LLM interactions.

🧩 How it works

  • Build MCP servers that expose tools, resources, and prompts to any MCP host.
  • Build MCP clients that connect to any MCP server.
  • Speak every standard transport: stdio, Streamable HTTP, and SSE.
  • Python 3.11+ is required.

⚙️ Key details

  • The cli extra adds the mcp command-line tool (mcp dev, mcp run, mcp install) on top of the SDK; install plain mcp if you don’t need it.
  • For one-off commands, uv run --with "mcp[cli]" mcp ... works without a project.
  • Example usage: Add two numbers or greet someone by name.
  • That’s a complete MCP server: one tool, one templated resource.
  • Call add with a=1, b=2 and you get 3 back.
  • Notice what you did not write: no JSON Schema (a: int, b: int is the schema), no request parsing, no validation code, no protocol handling.
  • Two type-hinted Python functions and a docstring.
  • The same package is a full MCP client.
  • A URL means Streamable HTTP, the transport you deploy.
  • Client can also launch a local server as a stdio subprocess or take any custom transport.

🚀 Availability

  • The project is licensed under the MIT License.
  • Contributions are welcome; see the contributing guide to get started.

💡 Why it matters

  • The SDK simplifies building and connecting to MCP servers and clients, reducing the need for manual request parsing, validation, and protocol handling.
  • It supports various transports, making it versatile for different deployment scenarios.
  • The project aims to support contributors of all levels of experience.

#PythonSDK #ModelContextProtocol #LLMApplications #AITools

Source: modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk

item.title: AutoGen 0.2 Course Requires Model Updates After OpenAI Deprecations
item.description:
AutoGen 0.2 Course Requires Model Updates After OpenAI Deprecations

A tutorial series built on AutoGen 0.2 (pyautogen 0.2.26) is now encountering model‑not‑found errors because many OpenAI models used in the lessons have been retired.

🔍 Overview

  • Course recorded on AutoGen 0.2; code unchanged.
  • The AutoGen 0.2 line is now maintained as AG2 (pip install ag2).
  • Several OpenAI models referenced in the lessons have been shut down.

⚙️ Key details

  • Python 3.11 or 3.12 required; pyautogen 0.2.26 does not support Python 3.13.
  • The pinned numpy version (1.26.4) provides wheels only up to Python 3.12.
  • Lessons 01‑08, 10, 11, 13, 14 reference retired models; lessons 09 and 12 use local or Hugging Face models and are unaffected.
Lesson Model status
01 Retired model
02 Retired model
03 Retired model
04 Retired model
05 Retired model
06 Retired model
07 Retired model
08 Retired model
10 Retired model
11 Retired model
13 Retired model
14 Retired model

🛠️ How to adapt the course

  • Change the model name in OAI_CONFIG_LIST.json and any "model": entries in .py files (search for gpt- and dall-e).
  • Delete temperature and max_tokens from the llm_config; GPT‑5 models use the default temperature and max_completion_tokens instead of max_tokens.
  • Use substitute models listed on the OpenAI deprecations page; for small demos gpt-5.4-mini costs $0.75 / $4.50 per 1 M input/output tokens (cheaper than gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-sol).
  • Expect a cost‑calculation warning from pyautogen 0.2 because its price table predates the newer models.

📚 Additional resources

  • Install requirements with pip install -r requirements.txt.
  • Install extra Reddit project packages (langchain-community, praw) via pip install -r 14-reddit-newsletter/requirements.txt.
  • Use PyCharm Community Edition IDE or Anaconda if preferred.
  • Join the Discord community for questions.
  • For the actively maintained AutoGen 0.7 API, see the TylerProgramming/ai GitHub repository.

#AutoGen #OpenAI #Python #AI

Source: tylerprogramming/autogen-beginner-course

item.title: Resolving Python 3.15 Dependency Errors Caused by Local uv.lock Files
item.description:
Resolving Python 3.15 Dependency Errors Caused by Local uv.lock Files

Switching to Python 3.15 can cause occasional dependency errors when local uv.lock files pin dependency versions that lack Python 3.15 wheels.

🔍 Overview

Running commands such as uv run pytest leaves uv.lock files in the local environment. Because these files are listed in .gitignore, they are not committed to repositories. However, they can cause build failures when the locked version of a dependency does not yet support Python 3.15.

⚙️ Key details

  • Library practices: Most library projects omit a uv.lock file so they do not lock dependency versions for downstream users.
  • Error cause: Running uv run pytest generates a local uv.lock file, which may pin a dependency version such as watchfiles==1.1.1 that lacks a Python 3.15 wheel.
  • Build failure error: A failure occurs during maturin.build_wheel because the configured Python interpreter version (3.15) is newer than PyO3’s maximum supported version (3.14).

💡 Resolution

When encountering this error, deleting the uv.lock file and running uv run pytest again usually fixes the problem.

#Python #uv #PyO3 #SoftwareDevelopment

Source: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file

item.title: LangGraph Tutorial Shows How to Build Stateful AI Agents in Python
item.description:
LangGraph Tutorial Shows How to Build Stateful AI Agents in Python

LangGraph, a framework for building stateful AI agents and multi‑step LLM workflows, now has a hands‑on tutorial that walks developers through creating a complete agent in Python.

🔍 Overview

  • Building an AI agent is more than connecting an LLM to a prompt.\
  • When an application must plan a task, call a tool, retain intermediate results, and use those results to produce an answer, the workflow becomes stateful.\
  • LangGraph is designed to manage that stateful execution.

🧩 How LangGraph Works

  • Graph model – The application is modeled as a graph of nodes and edges, with shared state used to store and pass information between steps.\
  • State – Shared data that nodes can read and update as the graph executes. The documentation advises keeping state focused on information that needs to persist between steps rather than storing derivable values.\
  • Node definition – A LangGraph node is a function that receives the current state and returns updates to that state. Nodes operate on the same state, so they do not need to manually pass values to one another.\
  • Node capabilities – Nodes can perform LLM calls, API calls, database operations, or other application logic.\
  • Execution control – Developers define what each step does, determine what happens next, and preserve relevant information throughout the workflow, providing explicit control over execution flow.

⚙️ Tutorial Highlights

  • The tutorial builds a small but complete AI agent with three nodes: Plan → Tool Call → Answer.\
  • Workflow steps:
    1. Accept a user request.\
    2. Create a structured plan.\
    3. Call a tool based on that plan.\
    4. Use the tool result to generate the final response.
  • The fixed workflow offers a simple foundation for understanding how LangGraph manages state, nodes, tools, and execution flow.
  • Implementation uses Python and an OpenAI‑compatible chat model through LangChain’s OpenAI integration.
  • Setup notes: set your API key as an environment variable; for real projects, store credentials through your environment or a secret‑management system rather than hard‑coding them.

🚀 Extending the Agent

  • The basic workflow can be extended with persistence and conditional routing, demonstrating more agentic behavior where the next step depends on the current state and model output.\
  • By the end of the tutorial, you have a working LangGraph application that can be further extended with additional tools, conditional routing, memory, human approval, or extra agent steps.

💡 Why It Matters

  • LangGraph is particularly useful when an AI application needs explicit control over its execution flow, making it well suited for tool‑using agents, conditional workflows, and stateful AI applications.\
  • Developers who want practical experience can explore Great Learning’s AI Agents in LangGraph and the Building Intelligent AI Agents course, which cover implementation, workflow design, and AI agent design patterns.

#LangGraph #AIAgents #StatefulAI #LLM #Python

Source: LangGraph Tutorial: Build a Stateful AI Agent

item.title: Introduction of Pydantic AI and Pydantic AI Harness
item.description:
Introduction of Pydantic AI and Pydantic AI Harness

Pydantic AI has been released as a Python AI SDK providing a typed, extensible agent loop where models can be changed via a string swap.

🔍 Overview

The SDK allows the same agent to run across various environments, including:

  • Web frontends
  • Terminals
  • Voice calls
  • Durable background queues
  • GitHub Actions
  • As a plain object called via run()

🧩 How it works

Component Function
Pydantic AI Python AI SDK for typed data extraction and agent loops
Pydantic AI Harness Provides capabilities for complex, long-running work including memory, guardrails, planning, and storage
Pydantic Graph Separate package for typed control flow
Pydantic Evals Separate package for testing agent behavior similar to pytest
Pydantic Logfire AI observability platform for the entire app
Pydantic AI Gateway Model key management with real-time cost monitoring and budget control
genai-prices Maintains current model pricing
Monty Sandboxed Python interpreter for running model-written code

⚙️ Key details

  • Capabilities: Pydantic AI includes image generation and embeddings. Pydantic AI Harness can be used to build a complete coding agent featuring workspace-rooted file access, an allowlisted shell, repo orientation, and context management for long sessions.
  • Integration: The Gateway supports self-hosting and uses plain OpenTelemetry instrumentation, ensuring compatibility with existing backends.
  • Scope: The system supports a range of use cases from simple typed data extraction to complex multi-agent collaboration.

#PydanticAI #Python #AIAgents #LLM #SDK

Source: pydantic/pydantic-ai
